arxiv-2003-05174.title: Delay-Adaptive Learning in Generalized Linear Contextual Bandits
arxiv-2003-05174.creator: Jose Blanchet, Renyuan Xu, Zhengyuan Zhou
arxiv-2003-05174.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Jose Blanchet, Renyuan Xu, Zhengyuan Zhou. In this paper, we consider online learning in generalized linear contextual bandits where rewards are not immediately observed. Instead, rewards are available to the decision maker only after some delay, which is unknown and stochastic. We study the performance of two well-known algorithms adapted to this delayed setting: one based on upper confidence bounds, and the other based on Thompson sampling.

arxiv-2104-02205.title: Attention Head Masking for Inference Time Content Selection in Abstractive Summarization
arxiv-2104-02205.creator: Shuyang Cao, Lu Wang
arxiv-2104-02205.description: Abstract How can we effectively inform content selection in Transformer-based abstractive summarization models? In this work, we present a simple-yet-effective attention head masking technique, which is applied on encoder-decoder attentions to pinpoint salient content at inference time. Using attention head masking, we are able to reveal the relation between encoder-decoder attentions and content selection behaviors of summarization models.

arxiv-2206-02473.title: Cosserat micropolar elasticity: classical Eringen vs. dislocation form
arxiv-2206-02473.creator: Ionel-Dumitrel Ghiba ​, Gianluca Rizzi ​, Angela Madeo ​ and Patrizio Neff ​
arxiv-2206-02473.description: Abstract In this paper we do a comparative presentation of the linear isotropic Cosserat elastic model from two perspectives: the classical Mindlin-Eringen-Nowacki description in terms of a microrotation vector and a new formulation in terms of a skew-symmetric matrix and a curvature energy in dislocation form.

arxiv-2207-01961.title: Neimark-Sacker bifurcation and stability analysis in a discrete phytoplankton-zooplankton system with Holling type II functional response
arxiv-2207-01961.creator: S.K. Shoyimardonov
arxiv-2207-01961.description: Abstract . In this paper, we study discrete-time model of phytoplankton-zooplankton with Holling type II predator functional response. It is shown that Neimark-Sacker bifurcation occurs at the one of positive fixed points for certain parameter chosen as a bifurcation parameter. The existence and local stability of the positive fixed points of the model are proved.

arxiv-2311-02362.title: Decoy Effect in Search Interaction: A Pilot Study DOI: 10.1145/1122445.1122456 Conference: EVIA ’23: The 10th International Workshop on Evaluating Information Access; December 12-15, 2023; Tokyo, Japan Woodstock ’18: ACM Symposium on Neural Gaze Detection, June 03–05, 2018, Woodstock, NY Price: 15.0
arxiv-2311-02362.creator: Nuo Chen, Jiqun Liu, Tetsuya Sakai, Xiao-Ming Wu
arxiv-2311-02362.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Nuo Chen, Jiqun Liu, Tetsuya Sakai, Xiao-Ming Wu. In recent years, the influence of cognitive effects and biases on users’ thinking, behaving, and decision-making has garnered increasing attention in the field of interactive information retrieval. The decoy effect, one of the main empirically confirmed cognitive biases, refers to the shift in preference between two choices when a third option (the decoy) which is inferior to one of the initial choices is introduced.

arxiv-2501-01559.title: K-ARC: Adaptive Robot Coordination for Multi-Robot Kinodynamic Planning
arxiv-2501-01559.creator: Mike Qin, Irving Solis, James Motes, Marco Morales, Nancy M. Amato
arxiv-2501-01559.description: Abstract This work presents Kinodynamic Adaptive Robot Coordination (K-ARC), a novel algorithm for multi-robot kinodynamic planning. Our experimental results show the capability of K-ARC to plan for up to 32 planar mobile robots, while achieving up to an order of magnitude of speed-up compared to previous methods in various scenarios.

arxiv-2505-00624.creator: Chaitali Bhattacharyya, Yeseong Kim
arxiv-2505-00624.description: Abstract Training large language models (LLMs) from scratch requires significant computational resources, driving interest in developing smaller, domain-specific LLMs that maintain both efficiency and strong task performance. Medium-sized models such as LLaMA ( Touvron et al. 2023b ; Touvron et al.

arxiv-2505-04769.title: Vision-Language-Action Models: Concepts, Progress, Applications and Challenges Journal: Proceedings of the IEEE
arxiv-2505-04769.creator: Ranjan Sapkota, Yang Cao, Konstantinos I. Roumeliotis, Manoj Karkee
arxiv-2505-04769.description: Abstract Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models mark a transformative advancement in artificial intelligence, aiming to unify perception, natural language understanding, and embodied action within a single computational framework. This foundational review presents a comprehensive synthesis of recent advancements in Vision-Language-Action models, systematically organized across five thematic pillars that structure the landscape of this rapidly evolving field.

arxiv-2510-09175.title: Beyond Pairwise Connections: Extracting High-Order Functional Brain Network Structures under Global Constraints
arxiv-2510-09175.creator: Ling Zhan, Junjie Huang, Xiaoyao Yu, Wenyu Chen, Tao Jia, College of Computer, Information Science, Southwest University, Chongqing, China
arxiv-2510-09175.description: Abstract Functional brain network (FBN) modeling often relies on local pairwise interactions, whose limitation in capturing high-order dependencies is theoretically analyzed in this paper. Meanwhile, the computational burden and heuristic nature of current hypergraph modeling approaches hinder end-to-end learning of FBN structures directly from data distributions.

arxiv-2511-19096.title: Can we detect treatment effect waning from time-to-event data?
arxiv-2511-19096.creator: Eni Musta, Joris Mooij Korteweg-de Vries Institute for Mathematics, University of Amsterdam
arxiv-2511-19096.description: Abstract Understanding how the causal effect of a treatment evolves over time, including the potential for waning, is important for informed decisions on treatment discontinuation or repetition. For example, waning vaccine protection influences booster dose recommendations, while cost-effectiveness analyses require accounting for long-term efficacy of treatments.

pmc-10623706.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). BackgroundThe COVID-19 pandemic has negatively affected the mental health of international migrant workers (IMWs). IMWs experience multiple barriers to accessing mental health care. Two scalable interventions developed by the World Health Organization (WHO) were adapted to address some of these barriers: Doing What Matters in times of stress (DWM), a guided self-help web application, and Problem Management Plus (PM +), a brief facilitator-led program to enhance coping skills.

pmc-11364745.title: Aggregation-induced C–C bond formation on an electrode driven by the surface tension of water
pmc-11364745.creator: Mengfan Li, Xu Cheng
pmc-11364745.description: Electrochemical organic synthesis is typically conducted in organic media. The solvent and related supporting electrolytes negatively affect the greenness of electrosynthesis. In this work, with 100% water used as the solvent, we realize aggregation-driven electrochemical radical cross coupling of unsaturated compounds driven by water tension.

pmc-11513987.title: The neurotrophic factor MANF regulates autophagy and lysosome function to promote proteostasis in Caenorhabditis elegans
pmc-11513987.creator: Shane K. B. Taylor, Jessica H. Hartman, Bhagwati P. Gupta
pmc-11513987.description: SignificanceDysregulation of protein homeostasis can lead to harmful protein aggregation, a hallmark of age-related diseases. The neurotrophic factor, mesencephalic astrocyte-derived neurotrophic factor (MANF), protects cells from such protein aggregates and promotes survival of neurons. Given MANF’s therapeutic promise, understanding its molecular mechanism is vital.

pmc-11527647.title: The vacuolar anti-Pseudomonal activity of neutrophil primary granule peptidyl-arginine deiminase enzymes
pmc-11527647.creator: Rory Baird, Azeez Yusuf, Luke Forde, Kerstin Pohl, Kevin Kavanagh, Fidelma Fitzpatrick, Debananda Gogoi, Emer P. Reeves
pmc-11527647.description: The role of neutrophils in host defense involves several cell processes including phagocytosis, degranulation of antimicrobial proteins, and the release of neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs). In turn, dysregulated cell activity is associated with the pathogenesis of airway and rheumatic diseases, in which neutrophil-derived enzymes including peptidyl-arginine deiminases (PADs) play a role.

pmc-11684542.title: Radiological Insights of a Complex Orbital Blow-Out Fracture
pmc-11684542.creator: Dania Ali, Omar Najim, Artur Wojciechowski
pmc-11684542.description: CT is the gold standard for evaluating orbital trauma, providing rapid and detailed imaging of bony structures, soft tissue, and the globe. This is crucial in assessing orbital trauma due to its potential to cause significant impairment of ocular function.

pmc-11715675.title: Understanding Challenges of Recruiting African Americans for Genomic Studies in Alzheimer’s Disease Beyond Trust
pmc-11715675.creator: Takiyah D Starks, Allison M Caban‐Holt, Kristy A Terrell, Jesseca Crawford, Ashley Gregory, Larry D Adams, Michael L Cuccaro, Jonathan L Haines, Christiane Reitz, Jeffery M Vance, Margaret A Pericak‐Vance, Goldie S Byrd
pmc-11715675.description: BackgroundBlack/African Americans (B/AAs) remain underrepresented in Alzheimer’s disease (AD) research and clinical trials. As a part of understanding genetics and genomics of AD, four U.S sites are recruiting 4,000 African Americans over age 60 for research participation. We identify challenges and propose solutions for recruiting AA’s using community based and grass roots efforts.

pmc-11888683.title: Leukemia’s Wake-Up Call – A Case Report of a Patient’s Journey
pmc-11888683.creator: Ryon Sam, Ann Maria Pappachan, Jasmine Podimon, Sunil Mathew, Anees Ahammed, Ashna Sara Mathew
pmc-11888683.description: A 26-year-old male complained of fever, right neck swelling, anorexia, and weight loss for 4 months. The patient noticed a right swelling in the root of the neck that progressed from 1 × 1 cm to 5 × 6 cm. We reported a Kikuchi-like acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) case.

pmc-12472696.title: Therapeutic Effect of Membrane Vesicle Drug Delivery Systems in Inflammatory Bowel Disease
pmc-12472696.creator: Zhe Zhao, Ziyun Li, Yihuang Gu, Renjun Gu, Antonio Lopalco, Augusto Pessina
pmc-12472696.description: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is a chronic, heterogeneous condition characterized by recurrent intestinal inflammation and sustained mucosal barrier damage, profoundly impairing patients’ quality of life and imposing a considerable socioeconomic burden. Current therapeutic options are often constrained by low oral bioavailability, pronounced systemic toxicity, and inadequate tissue specificity, limiting their ability to achieve precise and durable efficacy.

pmc-12523176.title: Lactylation-induced ALKBH5 targets RNF123 to worsen retinal Müller cell activation through PKM2-regulated Glycolysis in diabetic retinopathy
pmc-12523176.creator: Shasha Luo, Ye Sun, Yifan Hu, Yujia Xu
pmc-12523176.description: BackgroundUbiquitin ligase RNF123 affects a variety of pathological processes, but little is known about its regulatory mechanism. This study defined the regulatory mechanisms of RNF123 in Müller cell activation in diabetic retinopathy (DR).MethodsRNF123 expression was analyzed in the retina of DR patients and diabetic mice.

pmc-13067589.title: Response of gut microbiome and metabolomic profiles to POLYCAN, a β-glucan derived from Aureobasidium pullulans SM-2001 in beagles
pmc-13067589.creator: Vetriselvi Sampath, Kyejin Lee, Minjeong Kim, Young Suk Kim, Dae Hong Min, Kyudong Han, Sungbo Cho, Dae-Kyung Kang, In Ho Kim
pmc-13067589.description: BackgroundThe importance of glucan additives has been widely recognized in farm animals. Yet the precise role of POLYCAN, a β-glucan derived from the black yeast Aureobasidium pullulans SM-2001, remains limited in companion animals. Therefore, this study aims to evaluate its effect on performance, nutrient digestibility, hematology, and the gut microbiome and serum metabolites in beagle dogs.

pmc-13123458.title: Transient Absorption Spectroscopy of Blue Copper Sites in Divergent Protein Folds: Azurin Versus Multicopper Oxidase
pmc-13123458.creator: Luis Ignacio Domenianni, Patrycja Kielb
pmc-13123458.description: Blue copper proteins share a highly conserved type‐1 copper coordination that gives rise to characteristic spectroscopic signatures, yet they are embedded in evolutionarily divergent protein folds. pmc-13314379.title: Epigenetic landscape of synthetic human centromere core regions: CENP-A assembly and euchromatic modifications interdependently antagonize heterochromatin accumulation
pmc-13314379.creator: Junichiro Ohzeki, Akiko Watanabe, Jia Xian Lee, Chiharu Minami, Kazuto Kugou, Kyotaro Yamazaki, Kenta Shirasawa, Sachiko Isobe, Yusuke Endo, Yasuhiro Kazuki
pmc-13314379.description: Centromeres are specialized chromatin structures essential for equal chromosome segregation. The human centromeres are organized on a portion of homogeneously repeated DNA sequence and contains nucleosomes including centromere specific histone H3 variant CENP-A. Histone modifications around the CENP-A dense region are also thought to have important roles in centromere function.
